says: The EPIPE that lint:promise-types (in next/) and lint:dead (the @demlik/code-graph dependency) print inside a full pnpm lint is not a shutdown race: the box's memory cgroup OOM killer kills the TypeScript API child mid-run, the parent's blocked read fails with 'Unexpected EOF ... (killed by signal SIGKILL)', and the finally block's snapshot.dispose() then writes a 'release' request to the dead child's pipe, so its EPIPE replaces the real error. The cap is a cgroup v1 limit of 14,002,708 kB (13.35 GiB) on all of a session's commands together, which free(1) does not show; a lone full pnpm lint already peaks right at it.
proof: Installed code: typescript 7.0.2 dist/api/sync/api.js:196 Snapshot.dispose sends apiRequest('release'), which goes through dist/api/syncChannel.js:221 writeTuple and :495 writeSync on the child's stdin fd with no check that the child is alive; @typescript/native-preview 7.0.0-dev.20260707.2, which lint:dead uses, has byte-identical syncChannel.js and Snapshot. Our call: promise-types.ts:322-327 disposes and closes in finally blocks; code-graph 0.15.0 dist/index.js:9314 calls ctx.close() in finally, which disposes live snapshots at dist/chunk-3EVT6XKY.js:84 before it kills the server. No race: both dispose once, in order, on one thread. Runs at 2623b9f39: lint:promise-types alone 10 times, 0 failed (54 to 62 s). Full pnpm lint alone 3 times, 0 failed, lowest MemAvailable 1.7 to 2.0 GB of 15 GB, the promise-types tsc child the largest process at 2.8 to 3.1 GB RSS. SIGKILL of the API child 25 s into lint:promise-types alone printed the reported stack exactly (EPIPE, writeAllBuf, Snapshot.dispose, promise-types.ts:323:16); the same on lint:dead printed EPIPE from Snapshot.dispose under code-graph's close. Full pnpm lint beside one 3 GB holder: dmesg 'Memory cgroup out of memory: Killed process (node-MainThread)', constraint CONSTRAINT_MEMCG, 'memory: usage 14002708kB, limit 14002708kB', the holder taken. Beside a 1.5 GB holder: dmesg 'Killed process (tsc) anon-rss:2460648kB', and the run printed 'pnpm -s lint:promise-types (failed, exit 1)' with the EPIPE stack at promise-types.ts:323:16. memory.failcnt was 663,414: the cgroup sits at its limit often. Not the same root cause as 2026-11-16-promise-types-empty-tuple-panic (on fabrikalfa/reflect-rest at 4ba508a3b): with one uncommitted file holding Schema.Tuple([]) in next/packages/libfabrika/src, lint:promise-types failed with 'Error: panic: interface conversion: checker.TypeData is *checker.TypeReference, not *checker.TupleType' at promise-types.ts:234:27 and printed no EPIPE, because the API child sends the panic back as a request error (MSG_ERROR) and stays alive, so the dispose after it succeeds. The two meet only in one place: any death of the child, a panic that took the process down included, would show as this same EPIPE, because the finally block masks it.
cost: A second agent's compiler or tests in the same box pushes a full pnpm lint over the cap; the kernel kills the largest process, usually a TypeScript API child, and the part reads red with an EPIPE that names a shutdown write, not the kill, so each sighting is rerun and chased as a TypeScript bug. The memory reading (about 14 GB free) looked like proof memory was not the cause, but 14 GB is the cgroup limit itself. Smallest fix, two parts. First, our code: in promise-types.ts, make the release never replace the first error, for example Effect.acquireRelease for the API and snapshot with a release that catches and logs its own failure, so the message becomes 'Unexpected EOF while reading from child process (killed by signal SIGKILL)'; the same for code-graph's close is a change to our existing patches/@demlik__code-graph@0.15.0.patch plus an issue on kamp-us/demlik, after 0054's read. TypeScript is not patched: a dispose that fails on a dead child is not a bug proved here. Second, the cause: the existing box-memory ticket, where pnpm lint in a box runs the API-heavy parts (lint:dead, lint:promise-types and the other tsgo users) fewer at a time, or a box runs one code agent while lint runs.
